Without the cross-address restriction, unrelated real spends and outputs can share Actions, so the minimum Action count is the maximum of the numbers of real spends and real outputs. Under the restriction, a real spend and a real output can share an Action only if they use the same expanded receiver. When no such pairing is possible, the minimum Action count is instead the sum of those numbers. This increases transaction size and reduces the hiding of transaction arity provided by spend/output pairing. Same-receiver pairing and additional dummy Actions remain possible, so the public Action count does not uniquely determine the numbers of real spends and real outputs. Since the restriction applies to all
Actions, the resulting increase in Action counts is not by itself a wallet-specific fingerprint.
By preventing payments between users within the

, this ZIP encourages users to transfer their funds out of that pool. Such transfers reveal the net amount leaving the pool on-chain, regardless of its destination. Transferring a wallet's entire balance at once can therefore reveal that balance, and the amounts and timing of transfers can help link them.
